purpose: One name per question a public input answers. The Framework grew three different meanings under the word type, and a developer could not tell from the name which one a component meant. The axes below fix the question each name answers; the alias map records every legacy name that still works, so a rename never breaks a consumer.

axes.appearance: How the control looks: default, tonal, outline, link, surface, ghost, filled, bordered, segmented.
axes.status: What the control reports about the world: success, warning, error, info, neutral.
axes.kind: What the control carries or is: an icon, an avatar, a checkbox, a folder, a file.

rules: A new public input that answers one of these questions uses the axis name, never type.
A legacy name keeps working through the prop's aliases, and is listed here until it is retired.
The canonical name wins when both are set on the same element.
A component may carry several axes at once, because they answer different questions: a tag can be a checkbox (kind) reporting success (status) drawn as a ghost (appearance).

components.note: a destructive control is a status, not a colour role: `scheme` keeps saying which colour family a button takes and `status` says what it is about. Only `error` is painted -- a button that succeeds or warns is a colour with no meaning until a product asks for one.
the same split as buttons: the colour family stays `scheme`, what the control is about is `status`, and only the destructive one is painted.
the class verification's two looks by sf-input's names: bordered cells, or filled cells (sf-verification--filled).
the class accordion's appearances by name: default is the filled surface, outline and flush its two modifiers.
the class menu's presentations by name: default, documentation-tree and compact, its two modifiers.
segmented draws the same radiogroup as a sunken track with a plate under the selected segment (simai/ui-source#4); default keeps the joined outlined buttons.
`primary` was a colour role inside a list of statuses; it is answered as neutral, and info gained a fill it never had
the skeleton's `type` is not part of this axis: it marks a placeholder standing in for an icon, which combines with any shape, so merging it into kind would make two combinable answers exclusive
the split: `type` answered both questions from one list, and still does — a status word given as type reaches the status axis, a content word reaches the kind axis

the split: `scheme` mixed colour roles with status words. `scheme` is not retired — it keeps answering which semantic colour the badge takes — but a status word given there is routed to the status axis, and the CSS matches the canonical class beside the legacy danger
primary was a colour inside a list of statuses; here it meant info

not_an_axis.scheme: which colour family a control uses (primary, secondary, on-surface). It is not an appearance -- the same appearance exists in every scheme -- and it is not a status: what a control is about is the status axis.
not_an_axis.mode: how a control behaves rather than how it looks (a modal loading inline or over ajax, a dropdown selecting or tagging).
not_an_axis.native-type: the HTML type attribute of a native element, which belongs to the platform, not to us.

exempt_properties.reason: a lifecycle state of the data — auto, loading, populated, empty, error — not a status the control reports about the world. The word error appears in both, which is why the exemption is written down rather than inferred.
exempt_properties.kept_for: sf-table lives with Larena (package larena, the component folder in simai/larena-ui) since 2026-10-11, and no free component declares data-state. The exemption stays here because the package runs tests/public-api-axes.contract.test.mjs in its overlay of ui-source, against this file, and a package file may not replace a ui-source one.

exempt_properties.reason: the value names which icon set the glyph comes from — outlined, rounded, sharp — and the same word keys the loader's global default in SF_BOOT_CONFIG.icons.type, SF.Loader.getDefaultIconType and SF_ICON_TYPE. Renaming only the attribute would split one concept across two names, so this one is left alone deliberately.
a legacy name for file-size: the file's own size as text (12 KB), not a step of the size ladder. It is honoured and documented as legacy; a renderer passes file-size and never size.

size_ladder.note: A component uses the steps it needs, but it uses these names. `full` is not a step: it means as wide as the viewport.

name_aliases.note: `input-size` named the inner field's size; `size` is the name every field uses. Both reach the same field.

change_event.rule: Every form value control reports a committed change as `change` on its host, once per change made by the user. A value set from code is not a change. A native control's `change` bubbles from its inner input; a composite control dispatches a `change` CustomEvent on its host. Older names stay emitted with the same detail as aliases for as long as the change journal (contracts/changes/journal.json) keeps them in compatibility; the manifest marks `change` with `canonical: true` and each alias with `alias_of: "change"`.

aliases.note: Also emitted by select() and clear().
`sf-datepicker-change` was named the preferred event; `change` now is.
The legacy names also fire when a value is set from code; `change` does not.
